reading.body:
Pete Aguilar's AI record in this data is nine political committee contributions from technology companies and four recorded votes on AI-related bills, all between March 2025 and August 2026.

The money is consistent and small. Qualcomm, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, and Palantir committees gave between $1,000 and $5,000 each, with Amazon and Google each appearing twice. These are corporate PAC contributions, not personal donations, and the amounts are routine for a sitting member of Congress.

The votes are all yea votes on suspension motions, a procedure used for bills with broad support. The data does not include the text of H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, or S. 146, so it cannot show whether any of them touched compute, data centers, or grid policy. It also does not establish that any contribution preceded or influenced any vote, and the page itself states that placement in date order is not a claim of causation.

What the record does not contain matters as much as what it does. There are no committee hearings, no floor speeches, no letters to agencies, and no positions on power or permitting for data centers. For a site arguing that compute and the grid now bind AI, this is a funding and voting record only, and it says nothing about where Aguilar stands on the infrastructure that constrains the industry.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Pete Aguilar: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
